evidence.description: An individual D&T portfolio review linking planning, making, testing, evaluation and presentation to authentic work, with ownership/support, gaps, next target and actual banking record.

routes.Supported: Supported: match two records with staff.
routes.Independent: Independent: review each skill and help used.

vocab.definition: Our work that shows a skill.
Help used to do a task.
Done without help for that step.
Check work and plan what is next.
A clear next thing to work on.

cases.text: A marked plan has the learner’s actual measurements.
cases.fact: The record shows their marking work.
cases.next_step: Link it to planning and measuring; note support.
cases.staff_note: A staff-prepared blank is not evidence that the pupil marked it.

cases.text: A model was folded with an adult starting one crease.
cases.fact: The pupil and adult did different parts.
cases.next_step: Record the pupil’s making and the adult help.

cases.text: A test sheet records a slip at the first load.
cases.fact: An actual result and stop are recorded.
cases.next_step: Keep it and explain what it shows.
cases.staff_note: An unsuccessful model can still evidence testing and evaluation.

cases.text: The evaluation links a proposed change to a real observation.
cases.fact: The reason comes from the test.
cases.next_step: Keep the link; label the change as proposed.
cases.staff_note: Do not claim the improvement is proven without a retest.

cases.text: A presentation outline exists but no audience exchange is recorded.
cases.fact: Preparation is present; delivery is unconfirmed.
cases.next_step: Check for an authentic record or plan a later exchange.
cases.staff_note: Do not invent an audience or question.

cases.text: A folder contains a polished adult model with no pupil response.
cases.fact: The work belongs to an adult.
cases.next_step: Label it as a model and find the pupil’s own work.
cases.staff_note: Blank forms and adult answers do not prove attainment.

Gather authentic W2–W6 records. Provide the checklist and usual communication support. Staff have the approved evidence-storage route ready; do not create a public folder or login task.
Offer processing time, a quiet start and the usual communication support. Capture each learner’s own work. Read the Staff Answers before teaching.

Access and practice
Supported: match two records with staff. Independent: review each skill and help used. Aspire: explain a limit and a precise next step.

Model ownership checking on an adult example. Review the learner’s actual records one at a time; record support and gaps. Agree one skill target, receive the learner response and bank only checked items.

Begin evidence during practice and finish during capture. Accept speech, pointing, drawing, writing or usual AAC. Scribe exact words without supplying the assessed reason. No forced pair work or public performance.
Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries

No fabricated, copied or backdated learner evidence. Keep photos and work references in approved staff storage. No new build or load test is required. Any gap leads to a future support plan, not a false completion tick.
Assessment and feedback

Check each claimed skill against actual work and who did it. Keep honest not-yet or missing entries. Source award labels are preserved in school staff mapping and masked in Public; no unit criteria, registration or completion is inferred. Bank only real learner evidence and record actual location/status.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the school's evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Speaking listening and writing
Explain a strength with evidence, acknowledge support and state a next-step target. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own portfolio; no communication criteria are assigned here.

Model and hinge

Fictional review: Jo links a plan to measuring. The marked length shows what Jo measured. Jo records: an adult helped me hold the ruler. The test record is missing, so Jo marks a gap. Next step: find the real record with staff. Staff bank only checked work and record the gap.

Individual evidence key

Check each claimed skill against actual work and who did it. Keep honest not-yet or missing entries. Source award labels are preserved in school staff mapping and masked in Public; no unit criteria, registration or completion is inferred. Bank only real learner evidence and record actual location/status.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: A staff-prepared blank is not evidence that the pupil marked it.
Card B: Do not claim full independence.
Card C: An unsuccessful model can still evidence testing and evaluation.
Card D: Do not claim the improvement is proven without a retest.
Card E: Do not invent an audience or question.
Card F: Blank forms and adult answers do not prove attainment.
Common misunderstandings
Neatness is not the same as independence. A stopped test can still provide valid evidence. A filled checklist is not proof that every skill or award is complete.
Teaching boundary

No fabricated, copied or backdated learner evidence. Keep photos and work references in approved staff storage. No new build or load test is required. Any gap leads to a future support plan, not a false completion tick.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
